title: Prepare covariates

blocks.what_we_do: Join age and ten principal components ([PCs](docs/glossary.md#pca-pc)) to the IDs of the retained samples. Then check that no value is missing and that the table has full rank (explained below).
blocks.why: Covariates are extra measured factors, such as age. They adjust the comparison between cases and controls. PCs describe ancestry differences between people. If the covariates belong to the wrong samples, every test is wrong, yet the output still looks normal. A sample with a missing covariate is dropped from the model. [Collinearity](docs/glossary.md#collinearity) means that one column can be predicted exactly from the other columns. Then the model cannot give a single answer. Full rank means that no column has this problem. We check the IDs and the rank before the scan. PLINK reads sex from the PSAM file and adds it to the model.
blocks.you_need: The state saved at 5.7, the cohort eigenvectors (the PC values of each sample) from 5.7 and the metadata from 2.7.
blocks.command:
```{r s6-3}
psam <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), ".psam"))
pcs <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7", "pca"), ".eigenvec"))
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
a <- match(psam$IID, metadata$IID); b <- match(psam$IID, pcs$IID)
stopifnot(!anyNA(a), !anyNA(b), !anyDuplicated(pcs$IID))
covar <- data.frame(FID = psam$FID, IID = psam$IID, Age = as.numeric(metadata$Age[a]))
for (name in paste0("PC", 1:10)) covar[[name]] <- as.numeric(pcs[[name]][b])
stopifnot(!anyNA(covar))
design <- model.matrix(~ ., data = data.frame(SEX = as.numeric(psam$SEX), covar[, -(1:2)]))
stopifnot(qr(design)$rank == ncol(design))
names(covar)[1] <- "#FID"
guided_write(covar, guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"))
cat(nrow(covar), "complete covariate rows written\n")
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.3", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"), parent = "6.1")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable. This step needs no PLINK operation. The R chunk is the complete command.

R reads or calculates the values it shows. It does not change the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
1,811 complete covariate rows that match the samples, with Age and PC1 to PC10. There are no duplicate or unmatched IDs. The design has full column rank.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the expected values.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console log. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Why is a complete covariate table with the right number of rows not enough by itself?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The rows must belong to the correct sample IDs. Each row must match its own sample.

</details>
